narrative.overview: TakeFastNotes is an instrument, and the interface is a working sheet rather than a card pile. A sheet has one job: hold a short record and say what it is. The screen is built the way a printed register is built — a fixed column for the classification, a wide column for the words, a right column for the state and the clock, and hairline rules between the rows. Nothing floats, nothing is rounded enough to be a card, and nothing is decorated. Depth comes from a white panel on a cool grey ground, not from shadows. The second half of the world is the vocabulary: two taxonomies run through the product, so the system refuses to abbreviate. A kind is always written out in full, and every mark is accompanied by its meaning somewhere on the same screen. The first run is a legend card; after that, the marks carry their own explanation in the menu that opens them. One thing in the system is alive: the grammar strip under the capture field, where the three pieces of capture syntax fill with ink the instant the draft uses them.
keyCharacteristics: An achromatic shell; colour appears only where it carries information.
Words, not codes, everywhere a classification is shown.
A legend printed on the sheet, not hidden behind a disclosure.
Hairline rules, aligned columns, tabular numerals, small corners.
Motion is state feedback only: 120-180ms, one easing curve, no choreography.

rules.name: The Achromatic Shell Rule
rules.body: The chrome carries no hue. If a colour is not telling the reader what a note is or where it stands, it does not ship.

rules.name: The Word Beside The Swatch Rule
rules.body: A colour never appears alone. Every kind swatch is followed by the kind's full name; every stage colour is followed by the stage's name and an authored mark.

rules.name: The One Scale Rule
rules.body: The type scale is fixed in rem — never fluid, never clamp().

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Literal Rule
rules.body: Monospace means this is a literal token or a measurement. If a word is prose, it is set in Archivo.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface is flat at rest. Shadow appears only when something genuinely floats above the page.

dos: Do write every kind and status out in full, next to its colour.
Do put the legend on the same screen as the marks it explains.
Do keep the three grammar tokens visible under the capture field and light them up as the draft uses them.
Do use hairline rules and aligned columns to separate records.
Do set timestamps, counts and syntax tokens in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.
donts: Don't abbreviate a kind into a two-letter code; a code needs a decoder, and the reader is new to the vocabulary.
Don't put colour in the chrome, on a panel, or on a background.
Don't lift a record into a card: no shadow, no radius-heavy surface, no card grid.
Don't add a permanent banner to explain the syntax; teach it where it is used.
Don't introduce a second type voice, a second font file, or a network request to render the interface.
